single_proposed_factor.name: train-only mean-centered random contrast
single_proposed_factor.formula: I_new = uint8(round(clip(mu + alpha*(I-mu),0,255))); mu is per-image spatial grayscale mean, shared across replicated RGB channels
single_proposed_factor.placement: Training augmentation only, once per final training image after existing geometric/HSV operations and before tensor conversion. Preserve boxes and all baseline augmentations; no CLAHE.
single_proposed_factor.validation_and_inference: Unchanged original images and existing channel adaptation; no random contrast.
single_proposed_factor.rng_note: Use reproducibly seeded augmentation randomness; record exact implementation and worker behavior; avoid resetting global RNG.
single_proposed_factor.hypothesis: A small additional mean-centered contrast perturbation might improve val generalization, including faint defect sensitivity. This is a robustness hypothesis, not a proven explanation of baseline errors.
single_proposed_factor.why_this_instead_of_clahe: Evidence for a contrast-specific failure is weak; global deterministic CLAHE may amplify noise/texture and would require train/val/inference alignment. Train-only augmentation keeps deployed preprocessing unchanged.
single_proposed_factor.baseline_interaction: hsv_v=0.4 already changes brightness gain and absolute contrast; this adds a specifically mean-centered perturbation and must not be described as baseline having no contrast changes.

selection_rule: Compare both candidates on the identical frozen val protocol; use higher official val mAP50-95 as primary criterion, retain baseline on tie or deterioration. Report mAP50, fixed P/R/F1, within-class FN strata and FP diagnostics as secondary evidence; no extra search using test.
limitations: Single seed cannot establish statistical significance.
Local mean contrast is not a validated causal visibility measure.
Any gain cannot automatically be called industrial robustness or texture suppression.
No test predictions or metrics were examined for this decision.
